5ea856368603.text: From a signal to a fingerprint

a972a83907a7.text: One receptor channel is a measurement. Several channels together are a fingerprint. That is why a mixture is hard: the row can sit between two references without belonging cleanly to either.

6191e2db1074.text: This module is an educational simulation. It is not the AeroSense model, and it does not report experimental accuracy.

bd6a3f0fec91.text: A label is a claim about a pattern. It is not proof that the upstream measurement was good.

1b6b46895846.text: Insect-inspired pipelines often use an antennal-lobe-like contrast step and a mushroom-body-like sparse projection before a later readout. AeroSense may test whether those stages help. That test has to be empirical. This canvas cannot substitute for it.

ab9fe83e3ed7.text: A classifier sits at the end of a chain: biology reports fluorescence, hardware turns that into a calibrated signal, a model builds a representation, and a person sees risk information. If the first steps are noisy or unvalidated, the last step still produces a label.

be73d85ff0cd.text: Ablation turns a processing step off to test its contribution. A clearer sparse picture in this lesson is not evidence of published model performance.

0addb4ace9ff.text: Compare Sample A, Sample B and a mixture in raw, contrast-enhanced and sparse views. Add noise or disable a processing step. The resemblance is a teaching output, not a model score.

e182252a8dac.text: Sparse coding and contrast can make overlapping rows easier to tell apart in this sketch. Whether they help a real decoder still has to be shown with real measurements and validation.

ed5fb1e1d43e.text: Conceptual simulation — not the AeroSense model and not experimental data.

26bf16770126.text: A single odor is generally represented by what?

1f578b7bd929.text: A pattern of activity across multiple receptors, not one private switch.

29022fe79f8e.text: A single dedicated receptor that fires only for that odor.

432e4d5eae7c.text: An AI confidence percentage that exists before any receptor responds.

9058ce402375.text: Odor identity, when it can be recovered at all, is typically read from a combination of receptor responses. One channel is usually shared across odors; the row is the fingerprint.

4be6b8235c6d.text: Why use contrast enhancement or sparse representation in a pattern pipeline?

aa2993cef108.text: They magically name the odor, so validation is unnecessary.

6915cda09231.text: They can transform overlapping raw rows into representations that are easier for a later step to separate — still without proving a real model works.

b09f52e8433b.text: They replace the need to measure anything at the receptor.

d3b9683e933c.text: AL-like contrast and MB-like sparse codes are representation tools. They may make neighboring patterns easier to tell apart. Whether they help a real AeroSense model is an empirical question, not a property of the cartoon.

caaae1941ac0.text: Does AI automatically make a sensor result reliable?

fe72a1dd39ea.text: Yes. Once a classifier runs, the measurement quality no longer matters.

b8468c4d886a.text: No. Model output depends on measurement quality, validation, and appropriate data.

45416f189c62.text: Yes, if the interface prints a high-looking score.

243110cbf779.text: A classifier can only interpret the information it receives. Poor calibration, missing controls, or the wrong training distribution still produce a number or a label. Reliability is demonstrated by measurement quality plus validation — not by the presence of AI.

54ea5d25531e.text: After seeing an ambiguous mixture, what would you now refuse to conclude from a confident-looking label?

673a5e839f1a.text: AI cannot rescue bad measurements — it can only interpret the information it receives.
